title: Teamwork
examples: How can I make sure everyone gets a chance to talk in a group?
What is the difference between listening and waiting to speak?
If my team disagrees on an idea, what should we do first?

explain.say: Today we are learning about teamwork skills. These skills help groups work together well. Our first skill is understanding roles within a team.
A role is a job you do in a group. Every role helps the team reach its goal. For example, one person might be the timekeeper. This person keeps track of how much time the group has left.
The next important skill is active listening. This means really paying attention to what others say. For example, if your partner speaks, you should look at them and nod to show you hear them.

Our third skill is solving disagreements. Sometimes people have different ideas. When this happens, we must talk calmly to find a solution. For instance, if two people want different colours for a poster, you can suggest voting.

In real life, teamwork is needed everywhere. Imagine you are building a large tower with blocks. One person needs to be the builder, another needs to count the blocks, and a third needs to shout warnings about falling blocks. Everyone has a role.
A common mistake is interrupting when someone else is talking. To avoid this, try counting to three in your head before you speak. This gives you time to think clearly.

faq.q: What is the difference between a role and a job?
faq.a: A role is more about what you contribute to the group. A job is a specific task you complete. You might have a role that includes several jobs.
asks: What does it mean to have a role?
Is a role the same as a job title?

faq.q: How do I show I am actively listening?
faq.a: You can show you are listening by making eye contact. You can also repeat back what the person said in your own words. This confirms you understood them.
asks: What should I do when someone is talking?
Is nodding enough to show I am listening?

faq.q: What should we do if we cannot agree on anything?
faq.a: If you disagree, suggest a fair way to decide, like voting. Remember to focus on the idea, not the person who suggested it. Keep your voice calm.
asks: How do we solve arguments in a group?
What if voting does not work?

faq.q: Does everyone have to have a different role?
faq.a: No, sometimes people can have multiple roles. However, it is helpful if everyone focuses on one main role to keep things organized. Roles can change depending on the task.
asks: Can I do two roles at once?
Are roles fixed for the whole project?

faq.q: Is it okay to disagree with my team?
faq.a: Yes, it is very important to disagree respectfully. Disagreement shows you are thinking critically. You must always disagree with the idea, never with the person.
asks: Is it bad to have different opinions?
How do I disagree without sounding rude?

facts: A role defines a person's responsibility in a group.
Active listening means paying full attention to the speaker.
When solving disagreements, compromise is often the best outcome.
Good teamwork requires respecting every person's contribution.

quiz.say: When a group needs to decide on a theme, and two members suggest different themes, what is the best first step?
quiz.show: A. Immediately arguing for your favorite theme.

options.show: C. Ignoring the disagreement and moving on.

options.show: D. Telling the teacher to decide for us.

options.show: B. Suggesting a method like voting or listing pros and cons.
